title: Teaching outside your trained subject
hook: Many Australian secondary maths classes are taught by teachers trained in another subject. You are in good company, and your other subject is an asset.
coreIdeaMd:
Three things that help most when teaching out of field:

1. **Stay one unit ahead, not one lesson ahead.** Knowing where a topic is heading stops you being caught out.
2. **Learn the common errors before the content.** Knowing what students get wrong helps you teach it right.
3. **Use what you already know about teaching.** Routines, questioning and relationships transfer from any subject.

It is fine to say to a class "let's work that out together". Modelling how to get unstuck is good maths teaching.

checkItems.stemMd: Which of these helps most when you are new to teaching a subject?
options: Keeping one lesson ahead of the class
Knowing the common student errors in the topic
checkItems.answer: Knowing the common student errors in the topic
checkItems.feedbackCorrect: Yes. Knowing the errors lets you plan for them.
checkItems.feedbackIncorrect: Knowing the common errors helps you plan questions and responses. One lesson ahead is often not enough.

tryTomorrow: Find one colleague who teaches the same year level and ask them: "What do students usually get wrong in this topic?"
reflectPrompt: What strength from your own subject could you bring to your maths lessons this week?
